205	  //   the auto-select effect below picks a valid timeline

231	        const next = new URLSearchParams(current);
232	        next.set('timeline', settings.lastTimelineId!);
233	        return next;
234	      }, { replace: true });
235	      return;
236	    }
237	
238	    // Wait for the timelines list before deciding to auto-create — otherwise
239	    // we'd race the network and create a duplicate "Main timeline" on every
240	    // first visit to a project that already has timelines.
241	    if (timelines.isLoading || timelines.error || !timelines.data) {

246	    if (nextTimelineId) {

276	  }, [

39	  const pendingConfigRef = useRef<ResolvedTimelineConfig | null>(null);
40	  const flushDeferredConfig = (nextConfig: ResolvedTimelineConfig, delayMs: number) => {
41	    if (deferTimerRef.current) clearTimeout(deferTimerRef.current);
42	    if (delayMs <= 0) {

53	    }
54

56	    const delayMs = pendingConfigRef.current ? 0 : 150;
57	    pendingConfigRef.current = null;
58	    flushDeferredConfig(nextConfig, delayMs);

1	import { AbsoluteFill } from 'remotion';
2	import { memo, useMemo, type FC, type ReactNode } from 'react';
3	import { getAudioTracks, getVisualTracks } from '@/tools/video-editor/lib/editor-utils';
4	import { getTimelineDurationInFrames } from '@/tools/video-editor/lib/config-utils';
5	import type { ResolvedTimelineClip, ResolvedTimelineConfig, TrackDefinition } from '@/tools/video-editor/types';
6	import { AudioTrack } from '@/tools/video-editor/compositions/AudioTrack';
7	import { AudioAnalysisProvider } from '@/tools/video-editor/compositions/AudioAnalysisProvider';
8	import { EffectLayerSequence } from '@/tools/video-editor/compositions/EffectLayerSequence';
9	import { TextClipSequence } from '@/tools/video-editor/compositions/TextClip';
10	import { VisualClipSequence } from '@/tools/video-editor/compositions/VisualClip';
11	
12	const sortClipsByAt = (clips: ResolvedTimelineClip[]): ResolvedTimelineClip[] => {
13	  return [...clips].sort((left, right) => left.at - right.at);
14	};
15	
16	const renderVisualTrack = (
17	  track: TrackDefinition,
18	  clips: ResolvedTimelineClip[],
19	  fps: number,
20	) => {
21	  const sortedClips = sortClipsByAt(clips);
22	  if (sortedClips.length === 0) {
23	    return null;
24	  }
25	
26	  return (
27	    <AbsoluteFill
28	      key={track.id}
29	      style={{
30	        opacity: track.opacity ?? 1,
31	        mixBlendMode: track.blendMode && track.blendMode !== 'normal' ? track.blendMode : undefined,
32	      }}
33	    >
34	      {sortedClips.map((clip, index) => {
35	        if (clip.clipType === 'effect-layer') {
36	          return null;
37	        }
38	
39	        if (clip.clipType === 'text') {
40	          return <TextClipSequence key={clip.id} clip={clip} track={track} fps={fps} />;
41	        }
42	
43	        const predecessor = index > 0 ? sortedClips[index - 1] : null;
44	        const hasPositionOverride = (
45	          clip.x !== undefined
46	          || clip.y !== undefined
47	          || clip.width !== undefined
48	          || clip.height !== undefined
49	          || clip.cropTop !== undefined
50	          || clip.cropBottom !== undefined
51	          || clip.cropLeft !== undefined
52	          || clip.cropRight !== undefined
53	        );
54	        if (hasPositionOverride) {
55	          return (
56	            <VisualClipSequence
57	              key={clip.id}
58	              clip={clip}
59	              track={track}
60	              fps={fps}
61	              predecessor={predecessor}
62	            />
63	          );
64	        }
65	
66	        const effectiveScale = track.scale ?? 1;
67	        const needsScaleWrapper = effectiveScale !== 1;
68	        if (needsScaleWrapper) {
69	          return (
70	            <AbsoluteFill
71	              key={clip.id}
72	              style={{
73	                transform: `scale(${effectiveScale})`,
74	                transformOrigin: 'center center',
75	                overflow: 'hidden',
76	                isolation: 'isolate',
77	              }}
78	            >
79	              <VisualClipSequence
80	                clip={clip}
81	                track={track}
82	                fps={fps}
83	                predecessor={predecessor}
84	              />
85	            </AbsoluteFill>
86	          );
87	        }
88	        return (
89	          <VisualClipSequence
90	            key={clip.id}
91	            clip={clip}
92	            track={track}
93	            fps={fps}
94	            predecessor={predecessor}
95	          />
96	        );
97	      })}
98	    </AbsoluteFill>
99	  );
100	};
101	
102	export const TimelineRenderer: FC<{ config: ResolvedTimelineConfig }> = memo(({ config }) => {
103	  const fps = config.output.fps;
104	  const visualTracks = useMemo(() => [...getVisualTracks(config)].reverse(), [config]);
105	  const audioTracks = useMemo(() => getAudioTracks(config), [config]);
106	  const totalDurationInFrames = useMemo(() => getTimelineDurationInFrames(config, fps), [config, fps]);
107	  const audioClips = useMemo(() => {
108	    const audioTrackIds = new Set(audioTracks.map((track) => track.id));
109	    return config.clips.filter((clip) => audioTrackIds.has(clip.track));
110	  }, [audioTracks, config.clips]);
111	  const clipsByTrack = useMemo(() => {
112	    return config.clips.reduce<{
113	      regular: Record<string, ResolvedTimelineClip[]>;
114	      effectLayers: Record<string, ResolvedTimelineClip[]>;
115	      all: Record<string, ResolvedTimelineClip[]>;
116	    }>((groups, clip) => {
117	      groups.all[clip.track] ??= [];
118	      groups.all[clip.track].push(clip);
119	      if (clip.clipType === 'effect-layer') {
120	        groups.effectLayers[clip.track] ??= [];
121	        groups.effectLayers[clip.track].push(clip);
122	      } else {
123	        groups.regular[clip.track] ??= [];
124	        groups.regular[clip.track].push(clip);
125	      }
126	      return groups;
127	    }, { regular: {}, effectLayers: {}, all: {} });
128	  }, [config]);
129	
130	  const visualContent = useMemo(() => {
131	    let accumulated: ReactNode = null;
132	
133	    for (const track of visualTracks) {
134	      const trackContent = renderVisualTrack(track, clipsByTrack.regular[track.id] ?? [], fps);
135	      let lowerTrackContent: ReactNode = accumulated;
136	      const effectLayers = sortClipsByAt(clipsByTrack.effectLayers[track.id] ?? []);
137	
138	      if (lowerTrackContent && effectLayers.length > 0) {
139	        for (const effectLayer of effectLayers) {
140	          lowerTrackContent = (
141	            <EffectLayerSequence key={effectLayer.id} clip={effectLayer} fps={fps}>
142	              {lowerTrackContent}
143	            </EffectLayerSequence>
144	          );
145	        }
146	      }
147	
148	      accumulated = lowerTrackContent && trackContent
149	        ? <>{lowerTrackContent}{trackContent}</>
150	        : (trackContent ?? lowerTrackContent);
151	    }
152	
153	    return accumulated;
154	  }, [clipsByTrack.effectLayers, clipsByTrack.regular, fps, visualTracks]);
155	
156	  return (
157	    <AudioAnalysisProvider clips={audioClips} fps={fps} totalDurationInFrames={totalDurationInFrames}>
158	      <AbsoluteFill style={{ backgroundColor: 'black', overflow: 'hidden' }}>
159	        <AbsoluteFill style={{ justifyContent: 'center', alignItems: 'center' }}>
160	          <AbsoluteFill style={{ position: 'relative', overflow: 'hidden' }}>{visualContent}</AbsoluteFill>
161	        </AbsoluteFill>
162	        {audioTracks.map((track) => (
163	          <AudioTrack
164	            key={track.id}
165	            track={track}
166	            clips={clipsByTrack.all[track.id] ?? []}
167	            fps={fps}
168	          />
169	        ))}
170	      </AbsoluteFill>
171	    </AudioAnalysisProvider>
172	  );
173	});
174

## Remotion-Based Video Editor Architecture Report

I've completed a thorough exploration of the video editor. Here's what I found:

### 1. **Location: Video Editor UI**

**Main Entry Points:**
- `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh-workspace/reigh-app/src/tools/video-editor/pages/VideoEditorPage.tsx` (line 1) — Top-level page component; handles timeline list, creation, and routing to the editor
- `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh-workspace/reigh-app/src/tools/video-editor/components/VideoEditorShell.tsx` (line 1) — Main shell layout component; orchestrates the full editor UI
- `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh-workspace/reigh-app/src/tools/video-editor/contexts/VideoEditorProvider.tsx` (line 387) — Provider that wires all state and renders the lightbox overlay

**Key UI Components:**
- `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh-workspace/reigh-app/src/tools/video-editor/components/TimelineEditor/TimelineEditor.tsx` — Timeline canvas and interaction layer
- `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh-workspace/reigh-app/src/tools/video-editor/components/PreviewPanel/RemotionPreview.tsx` (line 1) — Remotion Player wrapper for rendering/playback
- `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh-workspace/reigh-app/src/tools/video-editor/components/PropertiesPanel/ClipPanel.tsx` — Multi-tabbed properties inspector for editing clip attributes
- `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh-workspace/reigh-app/src/tools/video-editor/components/PreviewPanel/OverlayEditor.tsx` — Canvas-based text/position editor overlay

---

### 2. **Architecture: Well-Structured but Coupled**

The editor is **modularized into logical concerns but tightly integrated** with the app. It's not a standalone library. Here's the structure:

```
video-editor/
├── pages/           # Entry point
├── contexts/        # State providers (VideoEditorProvider, DataProviderContext)
├── components/      # UI layers
│   ├── TimelineEditor/      # Timeline canvas + clip interaction
│   ├── PreviewPanel/        # Remotion Player + preview
│   ├── PropertiesPanel/     # Properties, effects, audio inspector
│   └── ...
├── hooks/           # Business logic (~72 hook files)
│   ├── timelineStore.ts     # Zustand store (state + ops)
│   ├── useTimelineState.ts  # Orchestrator hook
│   ├── useClipDrag.ts       # Drag gesture logic
│   ├── useClipResize.ts     # Trim/resize logic
│   ├── useClipEditing.ts    # Split, mute, delete, add text
│   ├── useTimelineHistory.ts # Undo/redo
│   ├── useTimelinePersistence.ts # Sync to Supabase
│   └── ... (audio, effects, import/export, etc.)
├── compositions/    # Remotion components (render tree)
│   ├── TimelineRenderer.tsx  # Root composition
│   ├── VisualClip.tsx        # Media playback + effects
│   ├── TextClip.tsx          # Text rendering
│   └── AudioTrack.tsx        # Audio playback
├── effects/         # Effect system (entrance, exit, continuous)
├── lib/             # Utilities (config, coord math, mobile interaction)
├── data/            # DataProvider interface + Supabase impl
└── types/           # TypeScript interfaces (TimelineClip, etc.)
```

**State Management:** Zustand store (`timelineStore.ts`) with three synchronized slices:
- **Data slice** — Timeline config, clips, tracks, resolved assets
- **Ops slice** — All editing operations (callbacks)
- **Chrome slice** — UI state (selection, panels, playback)
- **Playback slice** — Playback position, playback rate

All slices are kept in sync via `syncOpsSlice` / `syncDataSlice` in `VideoEditorProvider.tsx` (line 351–353).

---

### 3. **Remotion Packages Used**

From `package.json` (lines 49–51):
```
"@remotion/media": "^4.0.438",
"@remotion/player": "^4.0.434",
"@remotion/web-renderer": "4.0.438",
"remotion": "^4.0.434",
```

**Usage Pattern:**
- `Player` component wraps `TimelineRenderer` composition (PreviewPanel, line 129)
- `TimelineRenderer` uses Remotion's `AbsoluteFill` primitives for frame-based rendering
- Clips are rendered as frame-synchronized sequences with effects applied as wrappers
- Player events (`frameupdate`, `play`, `pause`) sync timeline UI playback state

---

### 4. **State Management Pattern**

**Primary:** **Zustand + React Context**
- Zustand store for persistent state (data, ops, chrome, playback)
- React Context for read-only provider access (`DataProviderContext`, `VideoEditorProvider`)
- React Query for async data (timelines list, effect definitions)

**Secondary:** Local component state for UI-only concerns (lightbox visibility, tabs, dialogs)

**Data Flow:**
1. Editor loads timeline via `DataProvider.loadTimeline()` → Zustand store
2. User interaction → hook (e.g., `useClipDrag`) → `applyEdit()` call
3. Edit patches the Zustand store immediately (optimistic)
4. `useTimelinePersistence` watches store and syncs to Supabase periodically
5. Undo/redo managed via `useTimelineHistory` with checkpoint support

---

### 5. **Editor Capabilities**

**Clip Operations:**
- ✅ Trim (drag clip edges)
- ✅ Move (drag clip across timeline)
- ✅ Split (split clip at playhead or cursor)
- ✅ Delete (single or bulk)
- ✅ Change clip speed
- ✅ Detach audio from video
- ✅ Mute / unmute clips
- ✅ Hold frames (pause a video)

**Positioning & Transforms:**
- ✅ Pan/zoom (x, y, width, height, crop)
- ✅ Track fit modes (cover / contain / manual)
- ✅ Track scale, opacity, blend modes
- ✅ Clip opacity, rotation (via custom effects)

**Effects & Animation:**
- ✅ Entrance effects (predefined + custom)
- ✅ Exit effects (predefined + custom)
- ✅ Continuous effects (predefined + custom)
- ✅ Transitions between clips
- ✅ Audio-reactive effects (via audio binding)
- ✅ Effect parameter controls (sliders, colors, dropdowns)

**Media & Assets:**
- ✅ Import images/videos (drag-and-drop or file picker)
- ✅ Register generation assets from app
- ✅ Asset registry with thumbnails
- ✅ Waveform visualization for audio
- ✅ Audio analysis (silence detection)

**Text:**
- ✅ Add text clips with font, size, color, alignment, bold/italic
- ✅ Edit text in overlay editor (canvas-based)
- ✅ Position text independently

**Timeline Management:**
- ✅ Multiple tracks (audio + visual)
- ✅ Add/remove tracks
- ✅ Reorder tracks
- ✅ Track volume control
- ✅ Pin "shot groups" (collections of clips across tracks)

**Playback & Export:**
- ✅ Play/pause/seek
- ✅ Playback rate control (via Player)
- ✅ Preview at composition resolution
- ✅ Render/export (via separate task system)

**Developer Features:**
- ✅ Undo/redo with history checkpoints
- ✅ Keyboard shortcuts (Cmd+Z, delete, etc.)
- ✅ Mobile interaction modes (browse, select, move, trim)
- ✅ Precision mode for fine editing
- ✅ Marquee selection
- ✅ Lightbox for media editing integration

---

### 6. **Separation of Concerns**

**Editor UI Layer** ↔ **App-Specific Features: TIGHTLY COUPLED**

**What IS Separated:**
- ✅ Data Provider interface (`DataProvider.ts`) — abstracted for testing
- ✅ Composition layer (`TimelineRenderer`, clips) — pure Remotion, no UI state
- ✅ Effects system — modular, compiled at runtime
- ✅ Utility lib (`editor-utils`, `config-utils`, etc.) — reusable

**What IS NOT Separated (Would Require Refactor):**
- ❌ Hard dependency on app auth, project context, generation system
- ❌ TypeScript types imported from `src/types/` (app-level types)
- ❌ Supabase integration baked into `SupabaseDataProvider`
- ❌ Media Lightbox integration (uses app-level `MediaLightbox` component)
- ❌ Task system integration (uses app-level task creation hooks)
- ❌ Hooks depend on shared contexts (`useAuth`, `useProjectSelectionContext`, `useShots`)
- ❌ No clear "edit surface" abstraction — everything flows through Zustand + VideoEditorProvider

---

### 7. **Reusability Assessment**

**Honest Verdict: 6/10 — Refactorable but Non-Trivial**

**Today (As-Is):**
- ❌ Not a standalone library
- ❌ Requires app infrastructure (auth, Supabase, project context, media system)
- ❌ Heavy integration into app state (e.g., AgentChat registration in provider)
- ⚠️ Would need environmental setup (custom effects, asset URLs) outside the app

**To Extract as Reusable:**
1. **Replace DataProvider** with a simpler abstraction (HTTP API or headless mode)
2. **Decouple Lightbox** — make media editing optional or use a callback
3. **Extract Remotion compositions** into a separate package (already ~80% decoupled)
4. **Externalize effects system** — it's already modular, but effect loading depends on Supabase
5. **Remove AgentChat bridge** — or make it a plugin
6. **Parametrize Supabase** — replace hard-coded references with DI or config

**Effort:**
- **Compositions alone:** 1–2 days (just copy `compositions/` + type defs)
- **Full editor UI:** 2–3 weeks (decouple hooks, replace data layer, fix type dependencies)
- **With effect system:** 3–4 weeks (add effect compilation layer, CDN/cache strategy)

**Low-Hanging Fruit:**
- The **Remotion composition tree** (`TimelineRenderer`, `VisualClip`, `AudioTrack`, `EffectLayerSequence`) is 80% reusable today — can be copied with minimal changes
- The **effect system** (`effects/`, `DynamicEffectRegistry`) is modular and could become a separate package
- The **hook library** is well-organized; extracting a subset (clip math, history, persistence) is straightforward

---

### Key Files Summary

| File | Purpose | Coupling |
|------|---------|----------|
| `VideoEditorPage.tsx` | Route, timeline selector | App context (routes, auth) |
| `VideoEditorProvider.tsx` | State + providers | App context, Supabase |
| `VideoEditorShell.tsx` | Layout orchestrator | Medium (uses panesStore) |
| `timelineStore.ts` | Zustand state machine | Low (pure state logic) |
| `useTimelineState.ts` | Hook orchestrator | High (pulls from 12+ sub-hooks) |
| `TimelineRenderer.tsx` | Remotion composition | Low (pure render logic) |
| `RemotionPreview.tsx` | Remotion Player wrapper | Low (just wraps Player) |
| `ClipPanel.tsx` | Properties inspector | Medium (app UI components) |
| `DataProvider.ts` | Interface (not impl) | Low (abstraction) |
| `SupabaseDataProvider.ts` | Persistence impl | High (Supabase-specific) |

---

**Bottom Line:** The editor is well-architected *for the Reigh app* but would require a **significant (3–4 week) refactoring** to become a truly reusable, app-agnostic component. The **Remotion compositions and effects system** are the reusable gems; the rest is app glue.

283	
284	`BREAKPOINT: <type>`
285	`Plan: <name>`
286	`State: <state>`
287	`Summary: <short reason>`
288	`Context: <artifacts, warnings, or the exact user decision needed>`
289	
290	Breakpoint types and triggers:
291	- `GATE_ESCALATE`
292	  Trigger: gate recommends `ESCALATE`, or `valid_next` offers `override add-note`, `override force-proceed`, or `override abort`.
293	- `GATE_BLOCKED`
294	  Trigger: you are in the `gate_proceed_blocked` branch and need the outer user to decide between more revision and `override force-proceed`.
295	- `EXECUTE_APPROVAL`
296	  Trigger: `finalize` succeeded in review mode and `execute` now requires explicit approval.
297	- `PHASE_ESCALATE`
298	  Trigger: a non-execute phase still fails after the required retry, or it returns unusable output twice.
299	- `EXECUTE_ESCALATE`
300	  Trigger: `execute` reaches the no-progress cap, or repeated blocking/timeouts prevent forward progress.
301	
302	## 6. Safeguards
303	Non-execute safeguards:
304	- If any non-execute phase fails, returns unusable output, or clearly lands in a bad session state, retry that same phase once with `--fresh`.
305	- If the exact same error appears twice in a row for the same phase, the next retry must use `--fresh`.
306	- If the phase still fails after the required fresh retry, stop with `BREAKPOINT: PHASE_ESCALATE`.
307	
308	Execute safeguards:
309	- Count whether each `execute` call creates forward progress.
310	- Forward progress means new completed tasks, a completed batch, or a state advance that clearly moves the run closer to done.
311	- If you hit 3 consecutive `execute` attempts without forward progress, stop with `BREAKPOINT: EXECUTE_ESCALATE`.
312	- If `execute` times out or is blocked, retry up to that same 3-attempt cap.
313	
314	Review safeguards:
315	- `needs_rework` is a normal workflow branch, not a phase failure.
316	- If `review` returns `needs_rework`, do not break out. Follow the rework loop and run `execute` again from `finalized`.
317	- If `review` returns blocked instead of a real verdict, the CLI keeps the run in `executed` with `next_step` set to `review`.
318	- If `review` returns blocked or otherwise unusable output, treat that as a review-phase problem and apply the non-execute retry rule.
319	
320	Notes and interruption safeguards:
321	- If the outer skill kills and relaunches you, start fresh with no reliable memory from the prior run.
322	- After any note injection or relaunch, run `megaplan status --plan <name>` immediately, read the full `notes` array, and treat all notes as context.
323	- Treat the most recent note as the relaunch explanation, then resume from `next_step`; the CLI state machine is the source of truth.
324	
325	## 7. Resume Protocol
326	When the outer conversation resumes you with `SendMessage`, or when a new subagent is launched on an existing plan:
327	1. Re-read the message carefully.
328	2. Run `megaplan status --plan <name>`.
329	3. Read the full `notes` array.
330	4. Resume from the current CLI state and `next_step`, not from memory.
331	
332	Resume rules:
333	- If the user grants execution approval, continue directly into `execute` with the correct approval flag.
334	- If the user answers a gate breakpoint, translate that answer into the minimum necessary action: continue revising, `override add-note`, `override force-proceed`, or `override abort`.
335	- If the user changes scope or intent materially, prefer `override replan`.
336	- After resuming, continue autonomously until the next defined breakpoint or completion.
337	
338	## 7A. Note Injection from Outer Skill
339	- Use the stored `PLAN_NAME` for note and status calls. If it was not captured, run `megaplan list` and fall back to the most recent plan.
340	- Classify the user message: "add context for next phase" -> Option A, "change direction NOW" -> Option B, "just a question" -> answer without touching the run. Default to Option A unless the message clearly demands interruption.
341	- Option A (inject-at-boundary): run `megaplan override add-note --plan <name> --note "<note>"`, confirm to the user, and do not `TaskStop` or `SendMessage`.
342	- Option B (kill+relaunch): `TaskStop` the orchestrator, run `megaplan override add-note --plan <name> --note "<note>"`, relaunch a new orchestrator with prompt `Resume plan <name>. Run megaplan status to get current state, read all notes, and continue from where it left off.`, then confirm to the user.
343	- Latency: Option A can take up to one phase boundary; if that is not acceptable, the user should ask for Option B.
344	
345	## 8. Execution Details
346	Finalize and execute:
347	- After `gated`, run `megaplan finalize --plan <name>`.
348	- In auto-approve mode, run `megaplan execute --plan <name> --confirm-destructive`.
349	- In review mode, stop with `BREAKPOINT: EXECUTE_APPROVAL`, then after approval run `megaplan execute --plan <name> --confirm-destructive --user-approved`.
350	
351	Per-batch execution:
352	- If the execution briefing or CLI response indicates per-batch execution, continue batch by batch.
353	- Batch numbering is global and 1-indexed.
354	- Use `megaplan progress --plan <name>` between batch executions.
355	- Re-run the same batch number after a timeout if needed; the harness will reconcile previously completed work.
356	
357	Execution loop end conditions:
358	- Continue until all actionable tasks are complete and the workflow reaches `done`.
359	- Stop early only for a defined breakpoint.
360	
361	## 9. Overrides & Plan Editing
362	Override rules:
363	- `megaplan override add-note` is safe from any active state when you need to record new user direction without changing state.
364	- `megaplan override force-proceed` from `critiqued` moves the run into `gated`. Use it only when the user clearly wants to override the gate.
365	- `megaplan override force-proceed` cannot bypass a missing project directory or missing success criteria.
366	- `megaplan override force-proceed` from `executed` moves the run to `done`. Use that only when the user explicitly accepts unresolved review issues.
367	- `megaplan override abort` ends the run. Use it only when the user clearly wants to stop.
368	- `megaplan override replan` is available from `critiqued`, `gated`, or `finalized`. Use it when the orchestrator itself needs to edit the plan directly instead of asking the revise worker to do it.
369	
370	Replan behavior:
371	- After `override replan`, read the latest plan file, edit it directly, then continue with `critique`.
372	
373	Step editing:
374	- `megaplan step add`, `step remove`, and `step move` are available while the run is in `planned`, `critiqued`, `gated`, or `finalized`.
375	- Use them when you need to insert, remove, or reorder step sections without hand-editing the markdown.
376	- After a step edit, re-check `status` and continue from the returned state.
377	
378	## 10. Completion Format
379	When the workflow completes, return exactly this shape:
380	
381	`COMPLETE: megaplan run finished`
382	`Plan: <name>`
383	`Final state: <state>`
384	`Summary: <outcome>`
385	`Artifacts: <key files or reports>`
386	`Follow-up: <only if something remains>`
387	
388	## 11. Command Reference
389	Core commands:
390	- `megaplan status --plan <name>`
391	- `megaplan progress --plan <name>`
392	- `megaplan audit --plan <name>`
393	
394	Workflow commands:
395	- `megaplan prep --plan <name>`
396	- `megaplan plan --plan <name>`
397	- `megaplan critique --plan <name>`
398	- `megaplan gate --plan <name>`
399	- `megaplan revise --plan <name>`
400	- `megaplan finalize --plan <name>`
401	- `megaplan execute --plan <name> --confirm-destructive`
402	- `megaplan execute --plan <name> --confirm-destructive --user-approved`
403	- `megaplan execute --plan <name> --confirm-destructive --user-approved --batch N`
404	- `megaplan review --plan <name>`
405	
406	Override and editing commands:
407	- `megaplan override add-note --plan <name> --note "..."`
408	- `megaplan override force-proceed --plan <name> --reason "..."`
409	- `megaplan override replan --plan <name> --reason "..." [--note "..."]`
410	- `megaplan override abort --plan <name> --reason "..."`
411	- `megaplan step add --plan <name> --after S<N> "description"`
412	- `megaplan step remove --plan <name> S<N>`
413	- `megaplan step move --plan <name> S<N> --after S<M>`
414	```

1	# Megaplan
2	Route every step through the `megaplan` CLI. Never call agents directly.
3	Before the first CLI call, resolve a working launcher and reuse it for the whole run. Do not assume `megaplan` itself is on `PATH`; command presence alone is not enough. Prove the launcher works by successfully running a harmless CLI call with it first. In the instructions below, treat `<launcher>` as that verified command.
4	Launcher resolution order:
5	1. Try `python -m megaplan config show`.
6	2. If that fails, try `./.venv/bin/python -m megaplan config show`.
7	3. If that fails, try `uv run python -m megaplan config show`.
8	4. If that fails, try a version-selected shim such as `PYENV_VERSION=3.11.11 megaplan config show`.
9	5. Only use bare `megaplan ...` if that exact form already succeeded during this check.
10	## Triage
11	Pick the right level based on the task:
12	- **Skip megaplan**: single-file fixes, bug fixes with clear cause, simple refactors, config changes, adding tests for existing code. Just do it.
13	- **Light**: multi-file changes with clear scope, well-understood features, straightforward additions. One critique pass, no gate, no review.
14	- **Standard** (default for megaplan): cross-cutting changes touching many subsystems, unfamiliar codebase areas, ambiguous requirements, changes with high breakage risk, or anything where the plan itself needs debate.
15	- **Heavy**: high-stakes changes where getting it wrong is expensive — security-critical code, data migrations, public API changes. Uses the same visible `prep` phase but with 8 critique checks instead of 4.
16	
17	Default to standard unless the task is clearly simple enough for light. Do not ask the user to choose robustness — pick it yourself based on the above. Only ask execution mode (auto-approve or review) when using megaplan.
18	## Start
19	Run `<launcher> config show` before `init`. If `raw_config.execution.auto_approve` is explicitly present, do not ask the execution-mode question and honor that configured override, including configured `false`. If that raw key is absent, ask execution mode (auto-approve or review) before `init`. In the same config check, respect `execution.robustness` as a settable override when it is configured; otherwise pick robustness yourself per the triage guidance above.
20	```bash
21	<launcher> init --project-dir "$PROJECT_DIR" [--auto-approve] [--robustness light|standard|robust|superrobust] "$IDEA"
22	```
23	Report the plan name, execution mode, robustness, current state, and next step.
24	## Workflow
25	Run the loop in this order:
26	1. `prep`
27	2. `plan`
28	3. `critique`
29	4. `gate`
30	5. `revise` when gate recommends iteration
31	6. `finalize`
32	7. `execute`
33	8. `review`
34	Use `next_step` and `valid_next` for CLI routing. After `gate`, follow `orchestrator_guidance` instead of manually interpreting gate signals. When a response includes `next_step_runtime`, use its `duration_hint` and `recommended_next_check_seconds` to calibrate timing.
35	At `--robustness light`, the loop is: `plan` → `critique` → `revise` → `finalize` → `execute`. There is no prep, no gate, and no review.
36	At `--robustness standard`, the loop is: `prep` → `plan` → `critique` → `gate` → ...
37	At `--robustness robust`, the loop is also `prep` → `plan` → `critique` → `gate` → ... but uses 8 critique checks instead of 4 and enables parallel critique.
38	At `--robustness superrobust`, the loop is the same as robust but also enables parallel review.
39	## Step Rules
40	- `plan`: inspect the repository first; produce the plan plus `questions`, `assumptions`, and `success_criteria`. Each criterion is `{"criterion": "...", "priority": "must|should|info"}`. `must` = hard gate (reviewer blocks), `should` = quality target (reviewer flags but doesn't block), `info` = human reference (reviewer skips).
41	- `prep`: make repository investigation explicit before planning. Respect `skip: true` when the task is already concrete enough.
42	- `critique`: surface concrete flags with concern, evidence, category, and severity; reuse open flag IDs; call out scope creep. Also validate that success criteria priorities are well-calibrated — `must` criteria should be verifiable yes/no, subjective goals should be `should`.
43	- `gate`: read the response, warnings, and `orchestrator_guidance`. (Skipped at light robustness.)
44	- `revise`: show the delta, flags addressed, and flags remaining. At light robustness, routes to `finalize`; otherwise loops back through `critique` and `gate`.
45	- `review`: judge success against the success criteria and the user's intent, not plan elegance. Only block on `must` criteria failures. `should` failures are flagged but don't require rework. `info` criteria are waived.
46	## Gate Principle
47	The gate response tells the orchestrator what to do next. Follow `orchestrator_guidance` unless you have a concrete reason to disagree after investigating the repository or plan artifacts yourself.
48	Investigate before disagreeing: read the current plan and critique artifacts, check the project code to verify whether a flagged issue is real, or use `megaplan status --plan <name>` / `megaplan audit --plan <name>`.
49	If you disagree with the guidance, explain why briefly and use an override. Do not manually reinterpret score trajectory, flag quality, or loop state when the gate already did that work for you.
50	## Execute
51	- After a successful gate, run `megaplan finalize` to produce the execution-ready briefing document.
52	- In auto-approve mode, run `megaplan execute --confirm-destructive` after finalize.
53	- In review mode, pause at the finalize-to-execute checkpoint and wait for explicit approval before running:
54	```bash
55	megaplan execute --confirm-destructive --user-approved
56	```
57	## Long-Running Execution
58	For plans with multiple batches, use per-batch mode to drive execution incrementally:
59	```bash
60	megaplan execute --plan <name> --confirm-destructive --user-approved --batch 1
61	megaplan execute --plan <name> --confirm-destructive --user-approved --batch 2
62	# ... continue until all batches complete
63	```
64	Between batches, poll progress:
65	```bash
66	megaplan progress --plan <name>
67	```
68	Use `megaplan status --plan <name>` for the full plan state, including active-step timing and any `next_step_runtime` guidance from the latest response.
69	Per-batch mode uses global batch numbering (1-indexed, computed from ALL tasks). Each `--batch N` call:
70	- Validates that batches 1..N-1 are complete
71	- Executes only batch N's tasks
72	- Writes `execution_batch_N.json` as evidence
73	- On the final batch, produces aggregate `execution.json` and transitions to `executed`
74	Timeout recovery: re-run the same `--batch N`. The harness checks prerequisite completion and merges only untracked tasks.
75	Note: `progress` shows completed state only (between-batch granularity). With per-batch mode, each batch is a separate CLI call, so the orchestrator has full visibility.
76	## Overrides
77	- `megaplan override add-note --plan <name> --note "..."`
78	- `megaplan override force-proceed --plan <name> --reason "..."`
79	- `megaplan override replan --plan <name> --reason "..." [--note "..."]`
80	- `megaplan override abort --plan <name> --reason "..."`
81	`force-proceed` is available from `critiqued` (routes to finalize, not execute). `replan` is available from `gated`, `finalized`, or `critiqued`. `add-note` is safe from any active state.
82	## Replan
83	Use `replan` when the orchestrator itself needs to edit the plan directly instead of asking the revise worker to do it.
84	```bash
85	megaplan override replan --plan <name> --reason "expanding scope" --note "Also clean up the display layer"
86	```
87	After `replan`, read the returned plan file, edit it directly, then run `megaplan critique`.
88	## Step Editing
89	Use `step` when you need to insert, remove, or reorder step sections (`## Step N:` or `### Step N:`) without hand-editing the markdown.
90	```bash
91	megaplan step add --plan <name> --after S3 "Add regression coverage for the parser"
92	megaplan step remove --plan <name> S4
93	megaplan step move --plan <name> S4 --after S2
94	```
95	Each edit writes a new same-iteration plan artifact, preserves the latest plan meta questions/success criteria/assumptions, and resets the plan to `planned` so it re-enters critique.
96	## Sessions And Autonomy
97	- Agents default to persistent sessions.
98	- `--fresh`: start a new persistent session.
99	- `--ephemeral`: one-off call with no saved session.
100	- `--persist`: explicit persistent mode.
101	- Keep moving and show results at each step.
102	- Only pause at finalize to execute in review mode.
103	## Configuration
104	View current defaults with `megaplan config show`. Override with `megaplan config set <key> <value>`. Reset with `megaplan config reset`.
105	When routing or behavior depends on config, check `megaplan config show` and respect user overrides instead of assuming defaults.
106	Settable execution keys: `execution.auto_approve`, `execution.robustness`.
107	## Commands
108	```bash
109	megaplan status --plan <name>
110	megaplan progress --plan <name>
111	megaplan audit --plan <name>
112	megaplan list
113	megaplan prep --plan <name>
114	megaplan plan --plan <name>
115	megaplan critique --plan <name>
116	megaplan revise --plan <name>
117	megaplan gate --plan <name>
118	megaplan finalize --plan <name>
119	megaplan execute --plan <name> --confirm-destructive [--batch N]
120	megaplan review --plan <name>
121	megaplan step add --plan <name> [--after S<N>] "description"
122	megaplan step remove --plan <name> S<N>
123	megaplan step move --plan <name> S<N> --after S<M>
124	megaplan override add-note --plan <name> --note "..."
125	megaplan override force-proceed --plan <name> --reason "..."
126	megaplan override replan --plan <name> --reason "..." [--note "..."]
127	megaplan override abort --plan <name> --reason "..."
128	megaplan config show
129	megaplan config set <key> <value>
130	megaplan config reset
131	```

1	<!-- Source of truth for Claude-specific subagent orchestration. Appended only to the Claude skill via bundled_global_file('claude_skill.md'). -->
2	## Subagent Mode
3	This appendix is Claude-specific. It adds a subagent path; subagent mode is the default for Claude.
4	
5	### Activation
6	- Default to subagent unless an inline override is explicitly set for this run or `megaplan config show` reports `"orchestration": {"mode": "inline"}`.
7	- Per-run override wins over config. If the run explicitly says `inline`, stay inline even when config prefers `subagent`.
8	- Use subagent mode for long multi-phase runs where keeping the outer conversation clean matters, especially auto-approve runs.
9	- Prefer inline mode for small edits, quick clarifications, or any run where the user wants to watch each phase in the main thread.
10	
11	### Launch
12	When subagent mode is active, the outer skill becomes a launcher plus breakpoint relay. Start a Claude Code Agent with:
13	- `description`: `Run megaplan autonomously for {PROJECT_DIR}`
14	- `prompt`: fill the template below with `{IDEA}`, `{PROJECT_DIR}`, `{AUTO_APPROVE}`, `{AUTO_APPROVE_FLAG}`, `{ROBUSTNESS}`, and `{ROBUSTNESS_FLAG}`
15	- `run_in_background: true` when `{AUTO_APPROVE}` is true; otherwise foreground is fine
16	- Expand `{AUTO_APPROVE_FLAG}` to an empty string when `raw_config.execution.auto_approve` is explicitly set; otherwise expand it to `--auto-approve` for auto-approve runs and an empty string for review runs.
17	- Expand `{ROBUSTNESS_FLAG}` to an empty string when `raw_config.execution.robustness` is explicitly set; otherwise expand it to `--robustness {ROBUSTNESS}`.
18	- After editing this source file, rerun `megaplan setup --force` so installed `SKILL.md` files pick up the refreshed appendix.
19	
20	### Outer Skill Handling
21	- Decide inline vs subagent before starting the workflow.
22	- In subagent mode, launch the agent, wait for either `BREAKPOINT:` or `COMPLETE:`, and keep the main thread thin.
23	- Support inject-after by letting the background subagent continue while the user runs `megaplan override add-note`; the next phase boundary picks it up from `megaplan status`.
24	- Support kill-and-inject by stopping the running subagent, appending a note with `megaplan override add-note`, and relaunching a new subagent on the same plan.
25	- When a breakpoint arrives, relay the summary to the user, collect the answer, and resume the same agent with `SendMessage` when possible.
26	- Parse only the explicit breakpoint header, not incidental text, when deciding whether the agent stopped intentionally.
27	- When completion arrives, report the final result back to the user without replaying every internal phase.
28	
29	### Agent Prompt Template
30	```text
31	You are the autonomous megaplan runner for this single run.
32	
33	Project: {PROJECT_DIR}
34	Idea: {IDEA}
35	Execution mode: {AUTO_APPROVE}
36	Robustness: {ROBUSTNESS}
37	
38	## 1. Role & Mission
39	Your job is to drive the megaplan workflow through the CLI until the run finishes or a defined breakpoint requires the outer conversation.
40	
41	Always follow these priorities, in order:
42	1. The latest user direction relayed through notes or resume messages.
43	2. The live CLI state from `megaplan status --plan <name>`.
44	3. The workflow and breakpoint rules in this template.
45	4. Your own memory of earlier turns.
46	
47	Always do these things:
48	- Operate through the `megaplan` CLI only. Do not call workers or agents directly.
49	- Keep the outer conversation clean. Do not ask for routine confirmation.
50	- Use `next_step` and `valid_next` for routing. If memory and CLI state disagree, trust CLI state.
51	- Follow `orchestrator_guidance` after `gate` unless you have a concrete reason to disagree after checking plan artifacts or repository evidence yourself.
52	- Treat user notes as authoritative.
53	
54	Never do these things:
55	- Do not run the workflow manually outside the CLI.
56	- Do not skip required phases for the selected robustness level.
57	- Do not emit a breakpoint unless one of the breakpoint rules below says to.
58	
59	## 2. Startup
60	Start the run like this:
61	1. Use empty-string expansion for `{AUTO_APPROVE_FLAG}` and `{ROBUSTNESS_FLAG}` whenever the corresponding `raw_config.execution` key is explicitly set.
62	2. Run `megaplan init --project-dir "{PROJECT_DIR}" {AUTO_APPROVE_FLAG} {ROBUSTNESS_FLAG} "{IDEA}"`.
63	3. Capture the returned plan name.
64	4. Output `PLAN_NAME: <name>` on its own line immediately after init and before any `BREAKPOINT:` or `COMPLETE:`.
65	5. Run `megaplan status --plan <name>`.
66	6. From then on, use that plan name for every command.
67	
68	At startup and after every later resume:
69	- Read `state`, `next_step`, and `valid_next`.
70	- If `notes_count > 0`, read the full `notes` array before acting. Do not track note cursors or indexes; always read the full array.
71	- Treat all notes as context. If the newest note changes direction, treat that note as the new intent and decide whether to continue, revise, replan, or break out.
72	- If `active_step` is present, treat it as an in-flight phase marker rather than a completed step. Use `last_step` for the most recent completed phase.
73	
74	## 3. Phase Routing by Robustness
75	Use the workflow below exactly.
76	
77	Light robustness:
78	- `init -> prep -> plan -> critique -> revise -> finalize -> execute -> done`
79	- There is no `gate`.
80	- There is no `review`.
81	- `prep` may return `skip: true`; that still counts as the visible prep phase.
82	- After the light `revise`, the CLI moves to `gated`, so the next command is `finalize`.
83	- After `execute`, the CLI will end the run.
84	
85	Standard robustness:
86	- `init -> prep -> plan -> critique -> gate`
87	- Then follow the gate decision tree below.
88	- `prep` may return `skip: true`; do not skip the command yourself.
89	- When you reach `gated`, run `finalize`.
90	- Then run `execute`.
91	- Then run `review`.
92	- If `review` returns `needs_rework`, the workflow becomes `finalized -> execute -> review` again until review passes or the CLI reaches its cap.
93	
94	Robust robustness:
95	- `init -> prep -> plan -> critique -> gate`
96	- `prep` may still return `skip: true`, but the phase remains visible in the CLI state/history.
97	- Uses 8 critique checks (vs 4 for standard) and enables parallel critique.
98	- After that, robust follows the same gate, finalize, execute, and review behavior as standard.
99	
100	Superrobust robustness:
101	- Same as robust, but also enables parallel review (review checks split across concurrent subagents).
102	
103	Gate decision tree for standard, robust, and superrobust:
104	- Condition 1: `gate_unset`
105	  Trigger: state is `critiqued` and `valid_next` includes `gate`.
106	  Action: run `megaplan gate --plan <name>`.
107	- Condition 2: `gate_iterate`
108	  Trigger: the latest gate recommendation is `ITERATE`, so `valid_next` includes `revise` but not `override force-proceed`.
109	  Action: run `megaplan revise --plan <name>`, then continue back through `critique` and `gate`.
110	- Condition 3: `gate_escalate`
111	  Trigger: the latest gate recommendation is `ESCALATE`, so `valid_next` offers `override add-note`, `override force-proceed`, or `override abort`.
112	  Action: stop with `BREAKPOINT: GATE_ESCALATE`.
113	- Condition 4: `gate_proceed_blocked`
114	  Trigger: the latest gate recommendation is `PROCEED`, but preflight still blocked execution, so state stays `critiqued` and `valid_next` offers `revise` plus `override force-proceed`.
115	  Action: do not finalize yet. Use `orchestrator_guidance` plus `preflight_results` to fix the blocking checks through `revise`. On iteration 1, the guidance text may stay generic, so inspect `preflight_results` yourself before revising. If the blocker cannot be resolved safely without a user decision, stop with `BREAKPOINT: GATE_BLOCKED`.
116	- Condition 5: `gate_proceed`
117	  Trigger: the latest gate recommendation is `PROCEED` and preflight passed, so state becomes `gated`.
118	  Action: run `megaplan finalize --plan <name>`.
119	
120	Review routing for standard, robust, and superrobust:
121	- If `review` succeeds, the run is done.
122	- If `review` returns `needs_rework`, the CLI moves back to `finalized` with `next_step` set to `execute`.
123	- When that happens, run `execute` again, then `review` again.
124	- This rework loop is capped by the CLI at {max_review_rework_cycles} `needs_rework` cycles. If the cap is hit, the CLI force-proceeds to done and records the issue.
125	
126	## 4. After Every Phase
127	After every phase command, immediately run:
128	`megaplan status --plan <name>`
129	
130	Then do all of the following before choosing the next command:
131	- Re-read `state`, `next_step`, and `valid_next`.
132	- If `notes_count > 0`, read the full `notes` array; worker agents already receive all notes automatically.
133	- Check whether the newest note changes direction before the next CLI call.
134	- If the last phase was `gate`, treat `orchestrator_guidance` as a literal routing hint. Its lead text will be one of these exact forms:
135	  `First iteration; follow gate recommendation: <recommendation>.`
136	  `Plan passed gate and preflight. Proceed to finalize.`
137	  `Gate says PROCEED but preflight blocked. Fix: <checks>.`
138	  `Gate escalated. Ask the user: force-proceed, add-note, or abort.`
139	  `Score plateaued with recurring critiques the loop can't fix. Consider force-proceeding: \`megaplan override force-proceed --plan <name>\``
140	  `Score improving (<previous> -> <current>). Continue to revise.`
141	  `Score worsening (<previous> -> <current>). Investigate; the loop may be diverging.`
142	  `Gate recommends another iteration. Revise the plan.`
143	- On iteration 1, the first form takes precedence over the more specific `PROCEED` or `ESCALATE` strings, so use `recommendation`, `valid_next`, and `preflight_results` together.
144	- If `orchestrator_guidance` includes extra text after that lead string, treat it as appended hints about unresolved flags, recurring critiques, or scope creep.
145	- If the phase response and `status` disagree, trust `status`.
146	- If the next move is unclear, prefer the explicit `valid_next` list over your own reconstruction of the state machine.
147	
148	## 5. Breakpoints
149	Use a breakpoint only for the cases in this section. Format every breakpoint exactly like this:
150	
151	`BREAKPOINT: <type>`
152	`Plan: <name>`
153	`State: <state>`
154	`Summary: <short reason>`
155	`Context: <artifacts, warnings, or the exact user decision needed>`
156	
157	Breakpoint types and triggers:
158	- `GATE_ESCALATE`
159	  Trigger: gate recommends `ESCALATE`, or `valid_next` offers `override add-note`, `override force-proceed`, or `override abort`.
160	- `GATE_BLOCKED`
161	  Trigger: you are in the `gate_proceed_blocked` branch and need the outer user to decide between more revision and `override force-proceed`.
162	- `EXECUTE_APPROVAL`
163	  Trigger: `finalize` succeeded in review mode and `execute` now requires explicit approval.
164	- `PHASE_ESCALATE`
165	  Trigger: a non-execute phase still fails after the required retry, or it returns unusable output twice.
166	- `EXECUTE_ESCALATE`
167	  Trigger: `execute` reaches the no-progress cap, or repeated blocking/timeouts prevent forward progress.
168	
169	## 6. Safeguards
170	Non-execute safeguards:
171	- If any non-execute phase fails, returns unusable output, or clearly lands in a bad session state, retry that same phase once with `--fresh`.
172	- If the exact same error appears twice in a row for the same phase, the next retry must use `--fresh`.
173	- If the phase still fails after the required fresh retry, stop with `BREAKPOINT: PHASE_ESCALATE`.
174	
175	Execute safeguards:
176	- Count whether each `execute` call creates forward progress.
177	- Forward progress means new completed tasks, a completed batch, or a state advance that clearly moves the run closer to done.
178	- If you hit {max_execute_no_progress} consecutive `execute` attempts without forward progress, stop with `BREAKPOINT: EXECUTE_ESCALATE`.
179	- If `execute` times out or is blocked, retry up to that same {max_execute_no_progress}-attempt cap.
180	
181	Review safeguards:
182	- `needs_rework` is a normal workflow branch, not a phase failure.
183	- If `review` returns `needs_rework`, do not break out. Follow the rework loop and run `execute` again from `finalized`.
184	- If `review` returns blocked instead of a real verdict, the CLI keeps the run in `executed` with `next_step` set to `review`.
185	- If `review` returns blocked or otherwise unusable output, treat that as a review-phase problem and apply the non-execute retry rule.
186	
187	Notes and interruption safeguards:
188	- If the outer skill kills and relaunches you, start fresh with no reliable memory from the prior run.
189	- After any note injection or relaunch, run `megaplan status --plan <name>` immediately, read the full `notes` array, and treat all notes as context.
190	- Treat the most recent note as the relaunch explanation, then resume from `next_step`; the CLI state machine is the source of truth.
191	
192	## 7. Resume Protocol
193	When the outer conversation resumes you with `SendMessage`, or when a new subagent is launched on an existing plan:
194	1. Re-read the message carefully.
195	2. Run `megaplan status --plan <name>`.
196	3. Read the full `notes` array.
197	4. Resume from the current CLI state and `next_step`, not from memory.
198	
199	Resume rules:
200	- If the user grants execution approval, continue directly into `execute` with the correct approval flag.
201	- If the user answers a gate breakpoint, translate that answer into the minimum necessary action: continue revising, `override add-note`, `override force-proceed`, or `override abort`.
202	- If the user changes scope or intent materially, prefer `override replan`.
203	- After resuming, continue autonomously until the next defined breakpoint or completion.
204	
205	## 7A. Note Injection from Outer Skill
206	- Use the stored `PLAN_NAME` for note and status calls. If it was not captured, run `megaplan list` and fall back to the most recent plan.
207	- Classify the user message: "add context for next phase" -> Option A, "change direction NOW" -> Option B, "just a question" -> answer without touching the run. Default to Option A unless the message clearly demands interruption.
208	- Option A (inject-at-boundary): run `megaplan override add-note --plan <name> --note "<note>"`, confirm to the user, and do not `TaskStop` or `SendMessage`.
209	- Option B (kill+relaunch): `TaskStop` the orchestrator, run `megaplan override add-note --plan <name> --note "<note>"`, relaunch a new orchestrator with prompt `Resume plan <name>. Run megaplan status to get current state, read all notes, and continue from where it left off.`, then confirm to the user.
210	- Latency: Option A can take up to one phase boundary; if that is not acceptable, the user should ask for Option B.
211	
212	## 8. Execution Details
213	Finalize and execute:
214	- After `gated`, run `megaplan finalize --plan <name>`.
215	- In auto-approve mode, run `megaplan execute --plan <name> --confirm-destructive`.
216	- In review mode, stop with `BREAKPOINT: EXECUTE_APPROVAL`, then after approval run `megaplan execute --plan <name> --confirm-destructive --user-approved`.
217	
218	Per-batch execution:
219	- If the execution briefing or CLI response indicates per-batch execution, continue batch by batch.
220	- Batch numbering is global and 1-indexed.
221	- Use `megaplan progress --plan <name>` between batch executions.
222	- Re-run the same batch number after a timeout if needed; the harness will reconcile previously completed work.
223	
224	Execution loop end conditions:
225	- Continue until all actionable tasks are complete and the workflow reaches `done`.
226	- Stop early only for a defined breakpoint.
227	
228	## 9. Overrides & Plan Editing
229	Override rules:
230	- `megaplan override add-note` is safe from any active state when you need to record new user direction without changing state.
231	- `megaplan override force-proceed` from `critiqued` moves the run into `gated`. Use it only when the user clearly wants to override the gate.
232	- `megaplan override force-proceed` cannot bypass a missing project directory or missing success criteria.
233	- `megaplan override force-proceed` from `executed` moves the run to `done`. Use that only when the user explicitly accepts unresolved review issues.
234	- `megaplan override abort` ends the run. Use it only when the user clearly wants to stop.
235	- `megaplan override replan` is available from `critiqued`, `gated`, or `finalized`. Use it when the orchestrator itself needs to edit the plan directly instead of asking the revise worker to do it.
236	
237	Replan behavior:
238	- After `override replan`, read the latest plan file, edit it directly, then continue with `critique`.
239	
240	Step editing:
241	- `megaplan step add`, `step remove`, and `step move` are available while the run is in `planned`, `critiqued`, `gated`, or `finalized`.
242	- Use them when you need to insert, remove, or reorder step sections without hand-editing the markdown.
243	- After a step edit, re-check `status` and continue from the returned state.
244	
245	## 10. Completion Format
246	When the workflow completes, return exactly this shape:
247	
248	`COMPLETE: megaplan run finished`
249	`Plan: <name>`
250	`Final state: <state>`
251	`Summary: <outcome>`
252	`Artifacts: <key files or reports>`
253	`Follow-up: <only if something remains>`
254	
255	## 11. Command Reference
256	Core commands:
257	- `megaplan status --plan <name>`
258	- `megaplan progress --plan <name>`
259	- `megaplan audit --plan <name>`
260	
261	Workflow commands:
262	- `megaplan prep --plan <name>`
263	- `megaplan plan --plan <name>`
264	- `megaplan critique --plan <name>`
265	- `megaplan gate --plan <name>`
266	- `megaplan revise --plan <name>`
267	- `megaplan finalize --plan <name>`
268	- `megaplan execute --plan <name> --confirm-destructive`
269	- `megaplan execute --plan <name> --confirm-destructive --user-approved`
270	- `megaplan execute --plan <name> --confirm-destructive --user-approved --batch N`
271	- `megaplan review --plan <name>`
272	
273	Override and editing commands:
274	- `megaplan override add-note --plan <name> --note "..."`
275	- `megaplan override force-proceed --plan <name> --reason "..."`
276	- `megaplan override replan --plan <name> --reason "..." [--note "..."]`
277	- `megaplan override abort --plan <name> --reason "..."`
278	- `megaplan step add --plan <name> --after S<N> "description"`
279	- `megaplan step remove --plan <name> S<N>`
280	- `megaplan step move --plan <name> S<N> --after S<M>`
281	```
282

1	# Megaplan
2	
3	A planning and execution harness that helps LLMs solve complex tasks through structured phases — plan, critique, gate, revise, finalize, execute, and review. Instead of one-shot attempts, Megaplan gives any model a rigorous process with independent critique and gating.
4	
5	## Quick Start — Claude Code / Codex
6	
7	Copy and give this to your agent:
8	
9	```
10	Please install megaplan and set it up for this project:
11	
12	pip install megaplan-harness
13	megaplan setup
14	
15	Once you're done, ask me what I need megaplan for.
16	```
17	
18	## Quick Start — Open Models via OpenRouter
19	
20	Copy and give this to your agent:
21	
22	```
23	Please install megaplan with the open-model backend and set it up:
24	
25	pip install megaplan-harness hermes-agent
26	
27	Then create ~/.hermes/.env with:
28	OPENROUTER_API_KEY=<my key>
29	
30	Then run: megaplan setup
31	
32	Once you're done, ask me what I need megaplan for.
33	```
34	
35	Get an OpenRouter key at [openrouter.ai/keys](https://openrouter.ai/keys). Any model on OpenRouter works — Qwen, Llama, Mistral, DeepSeek, etc.
36	
37	---
38	
39	## How it works
40	
41	```
42	plan → critique → gate → [revise → critique → gate]* → finalize → execute → review
43	```
44	
45	Each phase can use a different model. The critique phase uses an independent model to review the plan and raise flags. The gate decides whether to proceed or iterate. This prevents models from rubber-stamping their own work. Planning now goes through a visible `prep` phase so repository investigation is observable instead of hidden inside `plan`.
46	
47	## Running manually
48	
49	```bash
50	megaplan init --project-dir . "Fix the authentication bug in login.py"
51	megaplan plan --plan <name>
52	megaplan critique --plan <name>
53	megaplan gate --plan <name>
54	megaplan finalize --plan <name>
55	megaplan execute --plan <name>
56	```
57	
58	## Using different models per phase
59	
60	Models with provider prefixes route to direct APIs. Models without a prefix go through OpenRouter:
61	
62	```json
63	{
64	  "models": {
65	    "prep": "zhipu:glm-5.1",
66	    "plan": "zhipu:glm-5.1",
67	    "critique": "minimax:MiniMax-M2.7-highspeed",
68	    "execute": "zhipu:glm-5.1",
69	    "review": "minimax:MiniMax-M2.7-highspeed"
70	  }
71	}
72	```
73	
74	Configure direct provider keys in `~/.hermes/.env`:
75	
76	```bash
77	ZHIPU_API_KEY=...          # for zhipu: prefix
78	MINIMAX_API_KEY=...        # for minimax: prefix
79	GEMINI_API_KEY=...         # for google: prefix
80	```
81	
82	## Robustness levels
83	
84	- **light** — visible `prep` + one critique/revise pass, no gate or review
85	- **standard** — visible `prep` + 4 critique checks (default)
86	- **robust** — visible `prep` + 8 critique checks + parallel critique
87	- **superrobust** — same as robust + parallel review
88	
89	## Observability
90	
91	```bash
92	megaplan status --plan <name>
93	```
94	
95	`status` is the single monitoring command. It exposes lifecycle fields such as `active_step`, `last_step`, notes, cost, execute progress, and next-step runtime guidance.
96	`watch` remains as a backward-compatible alias to `status`.
97	
98	## Subagent mode (Claude Code / Codex)
99	
100	Subagent mode delegates the full workflow to an autonomous agent, returning control only at defined breakpoints. It is the default orchestration mode for Claude Code and Codex. Cursor continues to run inline.
101	
102	```bash
103	megaplan config set orchestration.mode subagent   # default
104	megaplan config set orchestration.mode inline      # switch back
105	```
106	
107	## Configuration & Defaults
108	
109	View all settings with `megaplan config show`. Override with `megaplan config set <key> <value>`. Reset with `megaplan config reset`.
110	
111	| Key | Default | Description |
112	|-----|---------|-------------|
113	| `orchestration.mode` | `subagent` | `inline` or `subagent` (Claude Code and Codex) |
114	| `orchestration.max_critique_concurrency` | `2` | Max parallel critique checks |
115	| `execution.worker_timeout_seconds` | `7200` | Worker process timeout (seconds) |
116	| `execution.max_execute_no_progress` | `3` | No-progress execute attempts before escalation |
117	| `execution.max_review_rework_cycles` | `3` | Review→rework loops before force-proceeding |
118	| `agents.<step>` | varies | Agent for each phase (`claude`, `codex`, `hermes`) |
119	
120	```bash
121	megaplan config set execution.worker_timeout_seconds 3600
122	megaplan config set agents.critique hermes
123	megaplan config reset
124	```
125	
126	## SWE-bench Experiment
127	
128	Megaplan is being tested live against Claude 4.5 Opus on SWE-bench Verified:

131	- **[hermes-megaplan](https://github.com/peteromallet/hermes-megaplan)** — experiment orchestration code

> DEVELOPER

You are the autonomous megaplan runner for this single run.

Project: /Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh-workspace
Idea: Design plan to extract the Remotion video editor (currently at reigh-app/src/tools/video-editor/) into a standalone, OSS-worthy repository, then wire the extracted package back into reigh-app to replace the in-tree editor. This is a doc-mode run — produce a rigorous design document, not code.

The design document must cover:

EXTRACTED REPO:
- Versioned, hand-editable TimelineConfig JSON schema as the core contract, with zod validators, JSON Schema export, and a migration function interface
- Pure Remotion engine package: (TimelineConfig, frame, assetResolver) -> pixels, no UI or host coupling — enables SSR / CLI / headless rendering
- React editor package using ports-and-adapters for: DataProvider (persistence), AssetResolver, MediaPicker, Exporter, HostContext config; each port ships a minimal in-memory default so the editor runs standalone
- CLI renderer: npx <name> render timeline.json out.mp4
- Examples: local-JSON editor, custom-backend adapter, headless render
- Deployable playground (Vercel)
- Pristine TS (no any), tree-shakeable ESM-first with CJS fallback, sourcemaps, narrow package.json#exports, changesets, tests on pure logic (schema migrations, store reducers, coord math)

REIGH-APP INTEGRATION:
- Reigh's current Supabase persistence becomes the reference custom DataProvider adapter living in reigh-app
- Reigh-specific concepts (shot groups, generation assets, AgentChat bridge, task-based export) must NOT live in extracted packages — they stay in reigh-app and consume the editor's public store/API
- Concrete migration plan: which files move, which stay, which split; post-change import shapes; order of operations that minimizes breakage
- How each host-specific touchpoint currently baked in (auth, projectId, MediaLightbox, AgentChat registration, task system) becomes an injected port or app-level layer

DESIGN DELIVERABLES:
- Final package layout (schema/engine/editor/cli) with rationale for each split
- Each port interface signature + in-memory default
- Timeline JSON format spec (versioning strategy, migration mechanics, app-specific vs core fields, forward-compat rules)
- Repo structure for the OSS repo (pnpm workspaces + Turborepo, examples/, apps/playground, docs site, CI)
- OSS polish checklist (license choice accounting for Remotion's licensing terms, README pitch, playground, docs site, release hygiene)
- Open questions & risks: Remotion license implications for downstream, schema stability commitment pre-1.0, how to keep extracted repo in sync with reigh-app during the transition, whether the engine boundary should abstract over renderers so Remotion could be swapped later

Execution mode: auto-approve (config.raw_config.execution.auto_approve is true)
Robustness: robust (8 critique checks + parallel critique — this is public API design, weeks of downstream refactor depend on it)

## 1. Role & Mission
Your job is to drive the megaplan workflow through the CLI until the run finishes or a defined breakpoint requires the outer conversation.

Always follow these priorities, in order:
1. The latest user direction relayed through notes or resume messages.
2. The live CLI state from `megaplan status --plan <name>`.
3. The workflow and breakpoint rules in this template.
4. Your own memory of earlier turns.

Always do these things:
- Operate through the `megaplan` CLI only. Do not call workers or agents directly.
- Keep the outer conversation clean. Do not ask for routine confirmation.
- Use `next_step` and `valid_next` for routing. If memory and CLI state disagree, trust CLI state.
- Follow `orchestrator_guidance` after `gate` unless you have a concrete reason to disagree after checking plan artifacts or repository evidence yourself.
- Treat user notes as authoritative.

Never do these things:
- Do not run the workflow manually outside the CLI.
- Do not skip required phases for the selected robustness level.
- Do not emit a breakpoint unless one of the breakpoint rules below says to.

## 2. Startup
Start the run like this:
1. Resolve a working launcher per the skill's resolution order:
   - Try `python -m megaplan config show`.
   - If that fails, try `./.venv/bin/python -m megaplan config show`.
   - If that fails, try `uv run python -m megaplan config show` (run from /Users/user_c042661f/Documents/megaplan or with appropriate cwd).
   - If that fails, try `PYENV_VERSION=3.11.11 megaplan config show`.
   - Only use bare `megaplan ...` if that exact form already succeeded.
   Prove the launcher works before the first real CLI call. Reuse the same launcher throughout. Earlier parent attempts: `python -m megaplan` failed (pyenv 3.8.10 has no module); `uv run python -m megaplan` from `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/megaplan` works.
2. Since raw_config.execution.auto_approve is explicitly set, expand {AUTO_APPROVE_FLAG} to an empty string. Since raw_config.execution.robustness is NOT set, expand {ROBUSTNESS_FLAG} to `--robustness robust`.
3. Run: `<launcher> init --project-dir [REDACTED] --robustness robust --mode doc --output docs/design/video-editor-oss-extraction.md "<IDEA>"`
4. Capture the returned plan name.
5. Output `PLAN_NAME: <name>` on its own line immediately after init and before any `BREAKPOINT:` or `COMPLETE:`.
6. Run `<launcher> status --plan <name>`.
7. From then on, use that plan name for every command.

At startup and after every later resume:
- Read `state`, `next_step`, and `valid_next`.
- If `notes_count > 0`, read the full `notes` array before acting. Do not track note cursors or indexes; always read the full array.
- Treat all notes as context. If the newest note changes direction, treat that note as the new intent and decide whether to continue, revise, replan, or break out.
- If `active_step` is present, treat it as an in-flight phase marker rather than a completed step. Use `last_step` for the most recent completed phase.

## 3. Phase Routing by Robustness
Robust robustness:
- `init -> prep -> plan -> critique -> gate`
- `prep` may still return `skip: true`, but the phase remains visible in the CLI state/history.
- Uses 8 critique checks (vs 4 for standard) and enables parallel critique.
- After that, robust follows the same gate, finalize, execute, and review behavior as standard.
- When you reach `gated`, run `finalize`.
- Then run `execute`.
- Then run `review`.
- If `review` returns `needs_rework`, the workflow becomes `finalized -> execute -> review` again until review passes or the CLI reaches its cap.

Gate decision tree:
- `gate_unset`: state is `critiqued` and `valid_next` includes `gate`. Run `gate`.
- `gate_iterate`: gate recommendation is `ITERATE`. Run `revise`, then continue back through `critique` and `gate`.
- `gate_escalate`: gate recommendation is `ESCALATE`. Stop with `BREAKPOINT: GATE_ESCALATE`.
- `gate_proceed_blocked`: recommendation is `PROCEED` but preflight blocked. Use `orchestrator_guidance` + `preflight_results` to fix via `revise`. If blocker cannot be resolved safely without a user decision, stop with `BREAKPOINT: GATE_BLOCKED`.
- `gate_proceed`: recommendation is `PROCEED` and preflight passed (state becomes `gated`). Run `finalize`.

Review routing:
- If `review` succeeds, the run is done.
- If `review` returns `needs_rework`, CLI moves back to `finalized` with `next_step=execute`. Run `execute` again, then `review` again.
- Capped by CLI at 3 `needs_rework` cycles.

## 4. After Every Phase
After every phase command, immediately run `<launcher> status --plan <name>`.

Then before choosing the next command:
- Re-read `state`, `next_step`, and `valid_next`.
- If `notes_count > 0`, read the full `notes` array.
- Check whether the newest note changes direction before the next CLI call.
- If the last phase was `gate`, treat `orchestrator_guidance` as a literal routing hint.
- If the phase response and `status` disagree, trust `status`.
- If the next move is unclear, prefer the explicit `valid_next` list.

## 5. Breakpoints
Use a breakpoint only when required. Format:

`BREAKPOINT: <type>`
`Plan: <name>`
`State: <state>`
`Summary: <short reason>`
`Context: <artifacts, warnings, or the exact user decision needed>`

Types: `GATE_ESCALATE`, `GATE_BLOCKED`, `EXECUTE_APPROVAL` (not applicable — auto-approve is on), `PHASE_ESCALATE`, `EXECUTE_ESCALATE`.

## 6. Safeguards
Non-execute: retry a failed phase once with `--fresh`. If same error appears twice, next retry must use `--fresh`. If still fails after fresh retry, stop with `BREAKPOINT: PHASE_ESCALATE`.

Execute: count forward progress. If 3 consecutive executes without forward progress, stop with `BREAKPOINT: EXECUTE_ESCALATE`.

Review: `needs_rework` is normal flow — follow the loop. If `review` returns blocked, apply the non-execute retry rule.

## 7. Resume Protocol
If resumed via SendMessage, re-read the message, run `status`, read full `notes` array, resume from current CLI state and `next_step`.

## 8. Execution Details
Finalize and execute (auto-approve mode):
- After `gated`, run `finalize`.
- Run `execute --confirm-destructive` (no `--user-approved` needed since auto-approve is configured).

Per-batch execution: if briefing or CLI response indicates per-batch, continue batch by batch. Use `progress` between batches. Re-run same batch number after timeout.

## 9. Overrides
- `override add-note` is safe from any active state.
- `override force-proceed` from `critiqued` routes to `finalize` (not execute).
- `override replan` available from `critiqued`, `gated`, `finalized`.
- `override abort` ends the run.

## 10. Completion Format
When the workflow completes, return exactly:

`COMPLETE: megaplan run finished`
`Plan: <name>`
`Final state: <state>`
`Summary: <outcome>`
`Artifacts: <key files or reports — include the path to the produced design doc at docs/design/video-editor-oss-extraction.md>`
`Follow-up: <only if something remains>`

## 11. Reference
Launcher resolution confirmed to work: `uv run python -m megaplan` from `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/megaplan`. Example full command:
`cd /Users/user_c042661f/Documents/megaplan && uv run python -m megaplan status --plan <name>`
...or use an absolute-path invocation if you prefer.

Core: `status`, `progress`, `audit`. Workflow: `prep`, `plan`, `critique`, `gate`, `revise`, `finalize`, `execute --confirm-destructive`, `review`. Overrides: `override add-note/force-proceed/replan/abort`. Step editing: `step add/remove/move`.

19	
20	# Video Editor Extraction Design
21	
22	## Executive Summary
23	
24	The current Remotion editor inside `reigh-app` is already substantial, but it is not packaged as a reusable product boundary. `VideoEditorPage` boots a host-specific `VideoEditorProvider`, which in turn wires the editor around `DataProvider`, project-scoped state, and host integrations rather than around an OSS contract surface [`reigh-app/src/tools/video-editor/pages/VideoEditorPage.tsx:182-325`][`reigh-app/src/tools/video-editor/contexts/VideoEditorProvider.tsx:387-403`][`reigh-app/src/tools/video-editor/data/DataProvider.ts:53-71`]. The current core type also still carries Reigh-specific state such as `pinnedShotGroups` in `TimelineConfig`, and the serializer rejects unexpected fields instead of preserving an extension namespace, which prevents clean host-specific metadata layering [`reigh-app/src/tools/video-editor/types/index.ts:172-186`][`reigh-app/src/tools/video-editor/lib/serialize.ts:98-122`]. Realtime behavior is similarly implemented today as a React Query cache-invalidation helper around a `realtimeEventProcessor`, not as a first-class provider subscription contract [`reigh-app/src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useTimelineRealtime.ts:29-43`].
25	
26	This design proposes a four-package extraction: `@tbd/schema` for a versioned hand-editable `TimelineConfig` contract, `@tbd/engine` for pure Remotion rendering, `@tbd/editor` for the React editor with injected ports, and `@tbd/cli` for headless rendering. Reigh-specific concerns such as shot groups, generation assets, AgentChat wiring, task-based export, auth, and project selection remain in `reigh-app`; the extracted packages expose stable contracts, store APIs, and extension slots rather than embedding those concerns in core. The result is a reusable editor that can run standalone with in-memory defaults, while Reigh keeps its current product-specific workflows by supplying adapters and extensions.
27	
28	The intended beneficiaries are two audiences. OSS consumers get a documented schema, a headless renderer, a standalone editor package, example apps, and a playground. Reigh engineers get a staged extraction path that minimizes breakage, preserves current behavior through compatibility shims, and makes host touchpoints explicit instead of implicit.
29	
30	This document does not propose a full non-linear editor replacement, a renderer-agnostic engine in v1, or a migration of Reigh-only product concepts into the extracted core. It assumes v1 remains Remotion-specific, keeps app-specific state behind a single `app` namespace in the schema, and treats the extraction as a packaging and boundary-hardening effort rather than a product redesign.
31

113	def set_work_dir_override(path: Path | str | None) -> None:
114	    """Set an explicit working directory for subprocess workers.

128	    Precedence:

# Video Editor OSS Extraction Design

This document describes how to extract `reigh-app/src/tools/video-editor/` into a standalone multi-package repository with four public packages: `schema`, `engine`, `editor`, and `cli`. The extracted packages must contain zero reigh-specific product concepts. Reigh-specific concerns remain in `reigh-app` and integrate through explicit ports or app-level extensions.

## Executive Summary

The current video editor is already close to a clean split in two important ways. First, the rendering path is materially separated: `TimelineRenderer.tsx`, `VisualClip.tsx`, `AudioTrack.tsx`, and `EffectLayerSequence.tsx` are Remotion-centric composition code with no direct Supabase, auth, or project selection imports (`reigh-app/src/tools/video-editor/compositions/TimelineRenderer.tsx:1-173`, `reigh-app/src/tools/video-editor/compositions/VisualClip.tsx:1-220`, `reigh-app/src/tools/video-editor/compositions/AudioTrack.tsx:1-68`, `reigh-app/src/tools/video-editor/compositions/EffectLayerSequence.tsx:1-65`). Second, the editor already has a store/provider seam: `useTimelineState()` creates and seeds a Zustand-backed external store, `TimelineStoreProvider` publishes it, and `VideoEditorShell` renders a propless `<TimelineEditor />` that reads selectors from the store (`reigh-app/src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useTimelineState.ts:413-838`, `reigh-app/src/tools/video-editor/hooks/timelineStore.ts:34-50`, `reigh-app/src/tools/video-editor/hooks/timelineStore.ts:302-550`, `reigh-app/src/tools/video-editor/components/VideoEditorShell.tsx:67-71`, `reigh-app/src/tools/video-editor/components/VideoEditorShell.tsx:686`, `reigh-app/src/tools/video-editor/components/VideoEditorShell.tsx:744`, `reigh-app/src/tools/video-editor/components/VideoEditorShell.tsx:770`).

The extraction problem is not rendering. It is host coupling. `TimelineEditor.tsx` currently imports project selection, shots context, shot creation/navigation, `VideoGenerationModal`, active task tracking, final-video availability, pinned shot-group hooks, stale-variant handling, and generation duplication utilities directly (`reigh-app/src/tools/video-editor/components/TimelineEditor/TimelineEditor.tsx:10-50`). `VideoEditorProvider.tsx` also binds the editor to `MediaLightbox`, `ShotsContext`, pending generation-add flows, and the app-level AgentChat bridge (`reigh-app/src/tools/video-editor/contexts/VideoEditorProvider.tsx:5-41`, `reigh-app/src/tools/video-editor/contexts/VideoEditorProvider.tsx:74-112`, `reigh-app/src/tools/video-editor/contexts/VideoEditorProvider.tsx:142-209`, `reigh-app/src/tools/video-editor/contexts/VideoEditorProvider.tsx:367-405`). The extraction therefore succeeds only if those concerns are removed from the packages and reintroduced through ports and extension slots.

Why extract:

- OSS audience: a versioned JSON timeline schema, a headless render engine, a reusable React editor shell, and a CLI renderer are independently valuable for teams building lightweight timeline tools.
- Reigh-app: smaller in-tree surface area, cleaner boundaries around Supabase/auth/project state, clearer test ownership, and the ability to consume the editor as a dependency instead of an in-tree subsystem.

Non-goals:

- This is not a general non-linear editor replacement.
- This does not abstract away Remotion in v1.
- This does not move reigh-specific workflow concepts into the OSS packages.
- This does not promise stable host extension APIs before the first schema and port contracts land.

Open placeholders to resolve during implementation:

| Placeholder | Proposed placeholder value | Why it remains open |
| --- | --- | --- |
| npm scope and package names | `@tbd/schema`, `@tbd/engine`, `@tbd/editor`, `@tbd/cli` | The final package scope depends on repo ownership and publishing setup. |
| GitHub org | `TBD` | Needed for README badges, docs URLs, and changesets publish config. |
| Remotion version pin | `Align to current reigh-app pin, then freeze at extraction cut` | Current reigh-app uses `remotion` `^4.0.434`, `@remotion/player` `^4.0.434`, `@remotion/media` `^4.0.438`, `@remotion/web-renderer` `4.0.438` (`reigh-app/package.json:45-72`). |
| OSS docs location | `apps/docs` in extracted repo | This reigh doc lives at `docs/design/video-editor-oss-extraction.md`; the standalone repo docs IA is still TBD. |

Callers should catch and fall back to drag-and-drop.\n- `open()` rejects with `PickerPermissionError` for denied OS-level file access. The editor treats this as non-fatal and surfaces a toast; timeline state is never mutated on picker failure.\n- All rejections must be `Error` subclasses with a `code` string. Hosts MUST NOT reject with raw strings or non-Error values.\n\nCurrent host coupling that motivates the port:"
